request: explain supply and demand with a graph

beats.intent: Axes of quantity and price with a falling demand line
beats.narration: As the price rises, people buy less: the demand line slopes down.
beats.code:
stage.title("Supply and demand")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 10), labels=("quantity", "price"))
demand = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda q: 9 - 0.8 * q, x_range=(0, 10), color=BLUE, label="demand")

beats.intent: A rising supply line crossing it
beats.narration: Sellers offer more when the price is higher: the supply line slopes up.
beats.code: supply = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda q: 1 + 0.8 * q, x_range=(0, 10), color=ORANGE, label="supply")

beats.intent: The crossing point (5, 5) marked as the market price
beats.narration: Where they cross, buyers and sellers agree: five units at a price of five.
beats.code:
eq = mark_point(stage, ax, (5, 5), color=YELLOW, label="(5, 5)")
stage.caption("The market settles where the lines cross")

beats.intent: The demand line shifted up and the new crossing at (6, 5.8)
beats.narration: If demand grows, its line shifts up. The new crossing is higher and further right: more sold, at a higher price.
beats.code:
demand2 = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda q: 10.6 - 0.8 * q, x_range=(0, 10), color=GREEN, label="more demand")
eq2 = mark_point(stage, ax, (6, 5.8), color=GREEN, label="(6, 5.8)")

request: if a price goes up 20% and then down 20%, is it back where it started?

beats.intent: A bar of 100 for the starting price
beats.narration: Start with a price of one hundred.
beats.code:
stage.title("Up 20%, then down 20%")
b = draw_bars(stage, [100], labels=["start"])

beats.intent: A second bar of 120 after the rise
beats.narration: Up twenty percent: one hundred and twenty.

beats.intent: A third bar of 96 after the fall, shorter than the first
beats.narration: Now down twenty percent, but of one hundred and twenty: that's twenty four off, leaving ninety six.
beats.code:
b3 = draw_bars(stage, [100, 120, 96], labels=["start", "+20%", "-20%"])
highlight(stage, b3[0][2] if len(b3) == 2 else b3[2], color=RED)

beats.narration: The two changes multiply: one point two times zero point eight is zero point nine six.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"100 \times 1.2 \times 0.8 = 96")
stage.caption("4% lower than it started")

request: what does the slope of a distance-time graph tell you?

beats.intent: Axes of time in hours and distance in km with a car's journey drawn
beats.narration: Here is a car trip: distance from home against time.
beats.code:
stage.title("Distance against time")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 4), y_range=(0, 200), labels=("hours", "km"))
trip = lambda t: 60 * t if t <= 2 else (120 if t <= 2.5 else 120 + 50 * (t - 2.5))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, trip, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The first steady stretch with its rise of 120 km over 2 hours marked
beats.narration: For two hours it climbs a hundred and twenty kilometres: a slope of sixty, which is sixty kilometres an hour.
beats.code:
run = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(0, 0), ax.c2p(2, 0), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 0), ax.c2p(2, 120), color=YELLOW)
stage.label(rise, "120 km", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("slope = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h")

beats.intent: The flat stretch from 2 to 2.5 hours lit as a stop
beats.narration: Then the line goes flat for half an hour: no distance gained. The car has stopped.
beats.code:
stop = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 120), ax.c2p(2.5, 120), color=RED)
stage.label(stop, "stopped", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The last stretch beside its slope, 50 km/h
beats.narration: The last stretch is less steep: fifty kilometres an hour. Steeper means faster.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\text{slope} = \frac{75}{1.5} = 50\ \text{km/h}")
stage.caption("Last stretch: less steep, so slower")

request: how does a bigger resistor change the current? Ohm's law

beats.intent: A battery and resistor loop drawn as a rectangle with a 12 V label
beats.narration: A twelve volt battery pushes current around a loop through a resistor.
beats.code:
stage.title("Ohm's law")
loop = draw_rectangle(stage, width=5, height=2.6, color=GREY_B, fill=0)
bat = draw_rectangle(stage, width=0.3, height=0.9, color=YELLOW, fill=0.8)
bat.move_to(loop.get_left())
stage.label(bat, "12 V", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)
res = draw_rectangle(stage, width=1.2, height=0.4, color=ORANGE, fill=0.6)
res.move_to(loop.get_top())
stage.label(res, "R", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: Dots flowing round the loop for the current
beats.narration: Charges flow round the loop. How fast depends on the resistor.
beats.code:
t = ValueTracker(0)
charges = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.08, color=YELLOW) for _ in range(12)])
charges.add_updater(lambda g: [d.move_to(loop.point_from_proportion((k / 12 + t.get_value()) % 1))
                               for k, d in enumerate(g)])
stage.add(charges)
stage.play(t.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
stage.caption("Current: charge flowing round the loop")

beats.intent: Bars of current for R = 2, 4 and 6 ohms: 6, 3 and 2 amps
beats.narration: With two ohms, six amps flow. Double the resistance to four: three amps. Six ohms: two amps.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [6, 3, 2], labels=["2 Ω", "4 Ω", "6 Ω"])
stage.caption("current in amps")

beats.intent: The bars beside I = V / R = 12 / R
beats.narration: Current is voltage divided by resistance: twelve over R.
